explanation: Reject source outcomes 6 and 7; return every remaining outcome unchanged.
correctness: Each accepted source value has the same probability 1/7. Conditioning on acceptance gives probability 1/5 for each result; repeated independent attempts preserve that distribution.
walkthrough: With injected draws 6, 7, 3, reject 6 and 7 and return 3. In general each accepted source value 1..5 has the same source probability, so conditioning on acceptance gives probability 1/5. The judge output true denotes passed range, source-use and probability properties, not a fixed rolled value. Rand5 has no value arguments and returns one integer 1..5. JSON contains a judge-only forced Rand7 draw prefix; expected true denotes random-source/range/distribution checks, not the rolled integer.
edgeCases: do not map rejected outcomes modulo five.
Any number of 6/7 draws must be rejected; returning draw modulo five would bias outcomes. Every call uses fresh supplied randomness.
timeComplexity: Expected O(1) time: each attempt succeeds with probability 5/7, so the expected number of source calls is 7/5. There is no finite worst-case call bound.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: retain only the current draw, regardless of the number of rejected attempts.
